messages:
sara: Heads-up — d-west2-1 dedicated pool spiking. GPU memory ~95% across most nodes, request queue +1.2k, we're seeing eviction churn on low-priority jobs. Anyone oncall?

miguel: @ryan are you around? I can join triage. :eyes:

ryan: I'm here, just grabbed coffee. Oncall page says control-plane latency for west2 is elevated (~2s). Might be API server slowness causing pod GC/backpressure.

ops-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool:d-west2-1 GPU_PRESSURE_HIGH 1719901234

ahmed: Can you paste the kube outputs?

miguel: quick snapshot:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -l pool=d-west2-1 -o custom-columns=NODE:.metadata.name,GPUMEM:.status.allocatable.gpuMemory,USED:...
NODE-01  16Gi  15.2Gi
NODE-02  16Gi  15.4Gi
NODE-03  16Gi  15.1Gi
...
$ kubectl get pods -n dedicated --selector=pool=d-west2-1 -o json | jq '.items|length'
1203
```

jia: yikes. Control-plane latency could explain why autoscaler can't react. If scale-up calls are queued, backlog grows and we hit mem pressure.

sara: Two constraints: 1) some enterprise orgs are dedicated-only and cannot be routed to hosted. 2) low-priority test orgs can fall back. Proposal: immediate traffic weight shift for non-enterprise orgs -> route 40% to hosted-west2, throttle dedicated-only tenants to rate-limit, and start preempting batch jobs.

ryan: Agree. Also we should avoid full drain ops since API is slow — prefer runtime-level weight switch via routing config. I'll push a conservative weight delta (40% to hosted) and warm up hosted pool.

miguel: Routing patch (will apply):
```json
{"route": "west2", "priorities": {"enterprise": 100, "standard": 60, "low": 40}, "fallback": "hosted-west2"}
```
Note: this is a live edit, will flip in 30s.

ahmed: Cost note — shifting ~40% estimated to add ~$16k/day on current query profile. We should monitor cost metrics and revert when safe.

ops-bot: DEPLOY: route-config updated by miguel at 1719901305

sara: miguel — confirm hosted warm-up status and any cold-start errors.

miguel: Hosted warm-up looks OK, added 24 nodes to hosted-west2 pool, primed with small requests. No 5xx so far but latencies ~320ms for hosted.

ryan: Throttled dedicated-only tenants to 60% of typical QPS as temporary measure. Added rate-limit rules: `org_allowance[enterprise] = 0.6 * baseline`.

jia: Seeing queue drop from 1.2k -> 300 within 2 min. Evictions reduced. Good signal.

sara: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) Open ticket for dedicated capacity commit bump with finance+sales. 2) Run a post-incident cost/latency analysis. Who owns?

miguel: I'll own the capacity ticket and coordinate sales.

ahmed: I'll run cost delta calc and post numbers in #finance.

ryan: I'll leave the routing in this conservative state for 2 hours and keep monitoring. If API server latency improves (<=200ms) we'll gradually shift weight back.

ops-bot: METRIC: dedicated-pool:d-west2-1 queue_length 1203 -> 298 (1719901400)

jia: Also discovered partial network flapping between k8s masters in west2 — opened infra-net incident. That explains control-plane slowness. Recommend maintenance window to replace affected control-plane NICs.

sara: OK schedule maintenance ASAP, but do it after traffic stabilizes. For now: keep hosted fallback, keep enterprise throttles, and communicate to CS about potential transient latencies.

miguel: I'll draft the CS blurb. Short notice: "We experienced degraded dedicated capacity in west2; workaround routing to hosted is active for non-enterprise traffic. Enterprise customers on dedicated are rate-limited temporarily."

ryan: If hosted latency drifts >450ms or 5xx increase >1.5x baseline, rollback routing to original weights and escalate to exec.

sara: Agreed. Add canary checks to automation: if hosted_error_rate > 1.5x or hosted_p95 > 500ms -> rollback.

miguel: Noted. I'll also collect logs for the evicted pods and share a short postmortem after the network patch.

ahmed: Cost estimate posted to #finance: ~16k/day for current shift. Will refine.

ops-bot: NOTE: Incident created INC-2024-567 by ryan at 1719901450

sara: Thanks team. Monitoring for next 2 hours. Miguel takes lead on capacity + CS comms, Ryan handles routing and rollback automation, Ahmed owns cost calc, Jia owns network incident.

miguel: On it. Will post updates every 15m or on significant changes. :thumbsup:

ryan: 1st update in 10m.

ops-bot: THREAD CLOSED (for archival) 1719901534
